title: Top-scorer strategy
intro: Merit = academics + written test (+ higher qualification). Your academics are already fixed, so the written test is where rank is decided. A pass (~50%) gets you on the list; the top ranks usually need 80%+. Everything below is aimed at that.

sections.heading: Target score sheet (aim: 85/100)
items: Non-technical sections (30 marks) are where toppers separate themselves: most candidates lose 8–12 marks there. Aim to drop no more than 4.
In Electrical, the gap between a pass and a top rank is roughly 15 questions — almost all of them classic, repeated concepts plus one-step numericals.

sections.heading: What to master first (by marks per hour of study)
items: 1. Power Systems (≈12 Qs): Ferranti, corona, skin effect, ACSR, SIL, insulators/string efficiency, per-unit, load/demand/diversity factor, HVDC, turbines, pf correction.

2. Electrical Machines (≈11 Qs): transformer OC/SC tests, losses, max efficiency, Buchholz/breather/conservator; slip, N_s, rotor frequency; DC series/shunt behaviour; synchronous V-curves and paralleling.
3. Protection & Switchgear (≈9 Qs): most common fault, symmetrical components, relay–application pairs, CT open-circuit rule, SF6/vacuum, arresters, earthing.
4. Circuits (≈9 Qs): Thevenin/max power, star–delta, 3-phase power, resonance, two-wattmeter.
5. WAPDA & power sector (≈6 Qs): pure memory — learn the dams table once and revise with flashcards. Cheapest marks in the paper.
6. Electronics & measurements, Power electronics, Control, EM (≈23 Qs combined): learn the formula sheet and the 'which instrument/device for what' pairs.

sections.heading: The 120-minute plan (72 s per question)
items: Pass 1 (0–70 min): answer everything you know at sight. Any numerical that will take more than ~90 s → mark your best guess, FLAG it, move on.
Pass 2 (70–105 min): return to flagged numericals using the palette.
Pass 3 (105–115 min): every unanswered question gets an answer. With no negative marking a blank is a guaranteed zero; a guess is worth 0.25 marks on average.
Last 5 minutes: do not change answers unless you find a clear error — first instincts on recall questions are usually right.
If negative marking is announced (check the call letter), guess only when you can eliminate at least two options.

sections.heading: Numbers to know by heart (saves minutes)
items: Synchronous speed at 50 Hz: 2-pole 3000, 4-pole 1500, 6-pole 1000, 8-pole 750, 10-pole 600, 12-pole 500 rpm.
Z_base = kV²/MVA; I_base = MVA/(√3 kV); fault MVA = base MVA / Z_pu.
Rectifiers: V_m/π (HW), 2V_m/π (FW), 1.35 V_L (3-φ bridge); ripple 1.21 / 0.482.

sections.heading: How examiners build options (and how to beat them)
items: Numericals: the distractors are your likely slips — missing √3, using V instead of V², forgetting ½, mixing line/phase, factor-of-10 unit errors. If your answer matches an option instantly, re-check the √3 and the unit once.
Concept questions: two options are usually clearly wrong; the remaining two differ in one word (minimum/maximum, series/parallel, lagging/leading, HV/LV side). Read the stem's key word twice.
'Most', 'NOT', 'except' questions cause most careless errors — underline them mentally.
AI-written variants reword classics: e.g. 'Ferranti effect is due to…' becomes 'Receiving-end voltage rise on an unloaded line is mainly caused by…'. Learn the reason, not the sentence.

sections.heading: Daily routine that gets toppers there
items: 50 questions a day (the dashboard target), mixing one strong and one weak topic.
20 flashcard reviews — 10 minutes, every day, no exceptions (spaced repetition only works if daily).
Read one notes page before practising that topic.
Re-attempt the mistake notebook every 2–3 days; it is your personal list of exam questions.
One full timed mock every week, then two in the final week. Review every wrong answer the same day.

sections.heading: Final 7 days
items: No new topics. Formula sheet every morning, flashcards every evening.
Mistake notebook to zero (or as close as possible).
Two full mocks at the same clock time as your actual test.
Re-check current affairs: Prime Minister, President, recent summits, sports winners, any new dams/projects in the news.
Day before: light revision only, sleep early. Carry the call letter, original CNIC and the exact items allowed by CTS.
